notes: PILOT: time segmentation, long training window. Stack on the base: python -m dskit.pipeline workflow configs/workflow.json --args configs/pilot-base.json --args configs/pilot-window-750.json. Every fold trains on the last 750 dates instead of 450 (about three years; the HAR literature's strongest rolling window is about 630 days, Audrino and Chassot 2024). It trades recency for sample size and leaves fewer scored folds. Step 3 refuses if fewer than warmup_folds + 1 folds fit before the holdout; if it does, lower train_n. Each window pilot changes three things at once: the training window, the warm-up years steps 4-6 select on (the fold grid is end-anchored), and the window of every reference, including horizon_empirical, the skill denominator. Skill against the references inside one run therefore does NOT answer recency against sample size. Compare RAW CRPS on the dates every window run scores (the 750 run's scored set is nested inside the 450 and 250 sets): read {work_dir}/step6/study_QQQ/evaluate/later/scores.parquet from pilot-base and both window runs, keep the common (quote_date, expiry) rows, and the raw variant only (scores carry a raw and a calibrated row per model), and compare each model's mean crps there. The six references have fixed specs, so they answer the window question cleanly; the step-6 candidate is selected on different warm-up years in each run, so its gap is directional only. The shared set is small (the 750 run's scored folds, roughly 160 dates on the earlier QQQ cohort) and has no interval: treat it as a screen.
